name: Visa de Residente (R) -- Por Tiempo Acumulado

requirement_groups.name: 2-year track (spouse of Colombian, parent of Colombian by birth/adoption, Mercosur migrant, Andean migrant)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 2 continuous years holding a valid Migrant (M) visa in one of these specific categories, immediately before applying.
requirements.fix_path: Hold the qualifying M visa continuously for 2 years.

requirement_groups.name: 5-year track (permanent partner, refugee, worker, partner/owner, independent professional, pensioner, investor, visa beneficiary)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 continuous years holding a valid Migrant (M) visa in one of these categories, immediately before applying. A salvoconducto (temporary bridging document) does NOT count toward this accumulation.
requirements.fix_path: Hold the qualifying M visa continuously for 5 years.

evidence_required.document: Copies of all prior M visas and salvoconductos held
Migration movement certificate from Migración Colombia

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (renewal of the card itself requested every 5 years; automatically lapses after 2 consecutive years of absence from Colombia)

sources.title: Abogados de Migración (immigration law firm) -- Visa R por tiempo acumulado: 2-year and 5-year tracks by prior M-visa category
Cancillería de Colombia -- Visa de Residente (tipo R): confirms 'por tiempo acumulado de permanencia' as one of 4 R sub-categories, open work permit, 5-year renewal cycle, 2-year absence lapse rule

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Colombia's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: the category's existence, the open-work-permit outcome, the 5-year renewal cycle, and the 2-year absence lapse rule are all confirmed directly at tier-1 (cancilleria.gov.co/node/26934) -- but the specific 2-year vs. 5-year breakdown by M-visa sub-category came only from a tier-3 immigration law firm's guide, since cancilleria's own resolución text (Resolution 5477 of 2022) could not be fully retrieved in this pass (truncated on fetch). required_prior_route_ids lists the M-visa-category routes built so far that plausibly feed into one track or the other; this dataset does not yet have route files for every M sub-category named in the tiempo-acumulado breakdown (e.g. independent professional, permanent partner as distinct from spouse) -- flagged as an incomplete cross-reference rather than silently narrowed.
